thread:
aline_sales: Borealis wants a short Private POC for our LLM inference. Their security team insists on L3 source preservation (for IDS), mTLS preferred, and as-tight-as-possible egress rules. They also want clarity on whether PrivateLink vs peering changes cost/SLA.

rob_se: Short take: mTLS = supported. PrivateLink is fastest and safest for locked-down VPCs but connector will SNAT so L3 src IPs are lost. Peering/TGW or direct routing preserves L3 src but needs route updates and symmetric return paths.

vijay_net: Tradeoffs and recommended approach: start with PrivateLink + static test EIPs for immediate functional tests (health checks, latency). If Borealis requires true L3 source preservation for IDS/audit, plan a quick follow-up for peering/TGW. Peering plan takes ~1-2 business days of design + infra ticket.

clare_platform: Pricing notes for sales: managed static egress IPs are an add-on: one-time provisioning fee + monthly per-EIP + small per-GB egress surcharge. If they commit to reserved capacity (12/24mo) we can include IPs at a discounted rate in the bundle. Peering itself doesn't change Redwood platform fees but cloud TGW/data charges may apply on their side.

aline_sales: They said X-Forwarded-For headers are unacceptable for audit. They need packet-level source preserved. Can we still demo anything quickly?

vijay_net: Yes — demo plan: 1) Provision PrivateLink and hand over test EIPs and short-lived mTLS certs for Borealis to validate connectivity and do functional tests. 2) Parallel: design peering route plan for L3 preserve. That keeps the POC moving while we work the network change.

rob_se: Minimal firewall allowlist sample for their team (please confirm final EIPs with infra before applying):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 52.210.77.45, 52.210.77.46 (Redwood test ENIs)
- Allow outbound TCP 8443 to: 52.210.77.47 (management plane, optional)
- DNS UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver or allowed DNS IP
- NTP UDP 123 (recommended for cert validation)
- Allow return ephemeral ports 1024-65535 if NATted
- Allow ICMP type 3/4 for PMTU discovery
```

clare_platform: MTU note: some SD-WAN appliances rewrite headers. Recommend testing with `ping -M do -s 1380 <peer-ip>` and enabling MSS clamp if they have MTU < 1400. Also ask them to check TLS handshake SNI and client cert CN during testing.

aline_sales: Borealis wants test EIPs + certs tomorrow AM. Any blockers?

infra-bot: heads-up: provisioning freeze on 2025-06-10 00:00-06:00 UTC may delay ENI/EIP creation if requested in that window.

vijay_net: I'll request test ENIs/EIPs now and aim to provide them before the freeze. We need Borealis firewall contact (engineer + egress IP) to coordinate.

rob_se: mTLS curl snippet we will provide (they'll get a short-lived client cert/key):
```bash
curl --cert boc-poc.crt --key boc-poc.key -v https://borealis.priv.redwood.ai:443/healthz
```
Non-mTLS quick check: `curl -v https://borealis.priv.redwood.ai:443/healthz`

clare_platform: For the security questionnaire: 1) KMS: customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; HSM-backed keys available under enterprise addendum. 2) Audit logs: request metadata (no raw payloads) can be exported to their S3/CloudWatch; payload logging can be disabled. 3) SOC2 report: available during enterprise negotiation. 4) TLS inspection: we do not intercept customer TLS; mutual TLS supported.

aline_sales: I'll loop in 'ops.borealis@borealis.bank' once we have EIPs. Thanks everyone.

vijay_net: Action items: 1) I'll share test EIPs + minimal allowlist by EOD, 2) Rob will prepare mTLS certs + curl examples, 3) Clare will send pricing delta for managed egress vs reserved bundle.

rob_se: No other blockers. If they confirm L3 preserve is mandatory we'll schedule the peering design review and notify infra.
